title: Structural Unemployment Risks for Singaporean PMETs Aged 40s and 50s
what_it_is: Structural Unemployment Risks for Singaporean PMETs Aged 40s and 50s

sections.label: Mid-career workforce support programmes
sections.summary: WSG and SSG programmes support mid-career jobseekers and mature workers, with over $10 billion invested in local workforce initiatives over five years.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: For example, Workforce Singapore's (WSG's) Mid-Career Pathways Programme and SkillsFuture Singapore's (SSG's) SkillsFuture Career Transition Programme support mid-career jobseekers to acquire industry relevant experience and skills to facilitate career transitions, while WSG’s Career Conversion Programmes provide employers with more salary support to reskill mature workers into growth job roles with good longer-term prospects.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: In total, we have invested over $10 billion over the last five years on local workforce initiatives to help our workers upskill and remain competitive.

sections.label: Tripartite Workgroup on Senior Employment
sections.summary: The Tripartite Workgroup on Senior Employment is studying recommendations for better support across a senior's career journey, to be released in the second half of this year.

sentences.text: The Tripartite Workgroup on Senior Employment is studying recommendations to provide better support across a senior's career journey, including during mid-career transitions and later-career stages.
Its recommendations will be released in the second half of this year.

sections.label: Helping employed professionals pivot
sections.summary: The Tripartite Workgroup for Senior Employment is looking at helping professionals still in employment understand where to pivot and guide their skills acquisition.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Indeed, that is one of the streams of work that the Tripartite Workgroup for Senior Employment is looking at.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: So, how can we help our professionals, even while they are still in employment, to try and understand better where they can pivot to, should there be a shift in the industry sector; and helping to guide them in that skills acquisition, in the looking out for opportunities and help them to navigate the kind of challenges that they may need to do in this transitional process?

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: So, going upstream, even to the age of 40s, for example, rather than wait till they are near retirement, or when they are retrenched.

sections.label: NTUC cross-sector worker movements
sections.summary: NTUC has a practice of helping workers potentially displaced from one union sector reach across unions in adjacent sectors through an internal arrangement.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: On the second question of whether we can facilitate more lateral movements across sectors, the Member looked at it from the union perspective, and in fact, in the National Trades Union Congress (NTUC), there has been a practice of helping workers who may potentially be displaced from one union sector to reach across other unions in the adjacent sector, and then facilitate their movements through an internal arrangement, because the unions in two different sectors may have more awareness of where the opportunities are.

sections.label: Tight labour market and awareness
sections.summary: The labour market is tight due to Singapore's resource constraints, and the key is raising worker awareness of adjacent-sector opportunities and helping them gain skills.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: The labour market is tight not because we want to facilitate lateral movements, but it is tight because we have resource constraints in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: But despite that tightness, I think the key thing is to make sure that there is more awareness amongst the workers themselves where opportunities may lie in adjacent sectors and have a system to help them gain the necessary skills so they can pivot across.
